summary: Barry County towersite acquired 1948-49; a 1961 survey describes a four-legged wooden tower about 90 ft tall; the page lists it as removed, undated.

facts.design: Four-legged wooden tower with a white observation room
facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts page lists the tower as removed. The page gives no removal date.

events.note: Missouri Conservation Commission acquired a 43-acre towersite in fiscal 1948-49. The 1949-50 state manual lists the site at 42.5 acres.
Major repairs made to the tower, per the fiscal 1956-57 Missouri Conservation Commission annual report.
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged wooden structure, overall height about 90 feet.
1974 USGS topographic map (published 1977) names the Jenkins Lookout Tower among the local landmarks.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1948-49 entry says the towersite was 43 acres when acquired. The 1949-50 state manual says 42.5 acres. Both figures are kept as reported; the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: One hobby site (Central US Lookouts) carries nearly all the detail: it quotes Missouri Conservation Commission annual reports, a 1961 Coast and Geodetic Survey record, and the official manual. The 1974 USGS map label is the only independent check, from Pastmaps. No build date, staffing, fire history or removal date was found. Searches also returned the MDC 2022 fire-tower article, which does not name Jenkins; a Missouri Life article that returned HTTP 403; and NHLR's Missouri list (20 lookouts), which does not include Jenkins. The 90-ft height is a 1961 survey figure. The brief's height_m was null, so the 27.4 m value is new and comes from that survey.
